purpose: Provide a stable, review-derived architecture contract for the seven frozen K501 Library Gateway registers and their bounded external-standard support direction, prior to register schema design.

frozen_by_parent_decision: Seven register names, count, and order.
K501 remains the native information model.
External standards use bounded, versioned adapters/interfaces.
Original data and derived representations remain separate.
Validation is not proof of truth.
defined_by_this_candidate: Reference direction convention and complete 7x7 relationship matrix.
Logical separation of Provenance and Rights record families within the one frozen register.
Scope rules for each support level.
authority_and_freeze_boundary.status_rule: This artifact is a Freeze Candidate only. It is not frozen, canonical, implemented, or integrated into Gateway v0.2.0.

registers.name: Directory Register
registers.responsibility: Keep source-scoped, time-bounded observations of directory and namespace structure, including observed locators, parent/child entries, entry kind, observation scope, observation window, warnings and non-atomicity.
owns: Directory observation records and their source/time context.
Observed path/locator and parent-child entry relationships.
Listing scope, counts, warnings, and atomicity limitations.
does_not_own: Stable K501 object identity.
Artifact identity, version semantics, or canonical status.
Proof that a target was read, semantically validated, or is currently resolvable.
registers.clarification: A locator records where an entry was observed at a stated time and source scope. It is not an identity. An observation may reference an independently established Object Identity record, but cannot create that identity from a path.

registers.name: Object Identity Register
registers.responsibility: Maintain K501 identity records for exact source-object instances and evidence-backed identity assertions while retaining each issuing source system’s native identifiers and distinctions.
owns: K501 object-identity records only under an explicitly approved identity rule.
Native source identifiers such as file_id and library_file_id together with their issuing source scope.
Evidence and status for supported identity, distinction, and unresolved-equivalence assertions.
does_not_own: Directory membership as its source of record.
Artifact descriptions or artifact-version declarations.
Read-completion, digest verification, rights decisions, or inferred equivalence based only on name/path/size/hash.
registers.clarification: The candidate identity subject is a source-object instance/occurrence, not a path, filename, semantic work, or digest. Equivalence across copies or revisions requires its own explicit evidence and approved rule. Native IDs remain source-scoped; a K501 ID does not replace them.

registers.name: Artifact Register
registers.responsibility: Describe identifiable digital artifacts and declared versions, formats, schemas, status claims, companion relationships, and references to the K501 object instances represented or contained.
owns: Artifact descriptors and artifact-version relationships.
Declared formats, media types, schema/version references, and source-scoped status claims.
Explicit links from artifact/version records to one or more object identities when evidenced.
does_not_own: The underlying source-object identity record.
Read-completion or byte-integrity evidence.
Canonical admission inferred from title, package presence, schema validity, or a mapped external representation.
registers.clarification: Artifact identity/version and source-object identity are separate domains. One artifact version may refer to one or more object instances; a source object may participate in more than one artifact description. Cardinality is recorded, never guessed.

registers.name: DeepRead Register
registers.responsibility: Record source-bound read events and coverage evidence, separating requested scope from the exact extent actually read, parsed, or visually inspected.
owns: Read-event records, method, time, and exact source scope.
Requested extent compared with completed extent.
Warnings, extraction limitations, unread ranges, deferrals, and coverage status.
does_not_own: Original source content as a replacement copy.
Semantic truth or completeness beyond the recorded method and extent.
Byte-integrity verification or rights clearance.
registers.clarification: A DeepRead record references the exact source-object identity and/or artifact version when available. Metadata listing, search snippets, and partial reads remain distinct from full content reads. DeepRead PASS is limited to the declared extent.

registers.name: Integrity Register
registers.responsibility: Record byte-integrity observations and verification events for an explicitly identified byte sequence, object instance, artifact version, payload, or package scope.
owns: Digest observations with algorithm and byte/scope definition.
Byte counts and verification results tied to the exact source object, artifact version, or package payload checked.
Integrity-event and verifier context.
does_not_own: Semantic truth, source authority, or identity equivalence.
Claims about bytes outside the declared digest scope.
Package-wide or Library-wide completeness without complete enumeration and verification.
registers.clarification: An Integrity record references the exact source identity and/or artifact version plus the byte scope. A matching digest proves byte equality only within that scope; it does not prove identity, meaning, completeness, permission, or canonicality.

registers.name: Provenance and Rights Register
registers.responsibility: Record source-to-derived relationships, activities, responsible agents, attribution, declared rights/licensing information, restrictions, and separately evidenced rights-review outcomes.
owns: Provenance relations and evidence linking source and derived object identities/artifacts.
Activity and responsible-agent references where supplied or evidenced.
Rights statements, license evidence, restrictions, rights-review state, and separately authorized redistribution decisions.
does_not_own: K501 object-identity assignment.
Legal conclusions inferred from technical accessibility, package validity, metadata, or a license label alone.
DeepRead coverage, integrity verification, or adapter validation as their source of record.
registers.clarification: The frozen combined register contains two logically distinct record families: PROVENANCE records and RIGHTS records. They share a register boundary but must not collapse into one assertion. Rights scope, evidence, restrictions, jurisdiction/authority where known, and review outcome remain explicit; UNKNOWN/OPEN is preserved.

registers.name: Route Registry
registers.responsibility: Maintain explicit, versionable navigation and resolution routes to registered directories, objects, artifact versions, or declared operations, including unresolved, stale, and expired routes.
owns: Route identifiers, route purpose, scope, and source/target declarations.
Target locators and target identity/artifact references when available.
Time-scoped route-resolution observations and unresolved/expired conditions.
does_not_own: Target object identity or artifact content.
Content validation, authorization, access rights, or semantic correctness.
The assertion that every declared target currently exists or is accessible.
registers.clarification: A route is a navigation contract. Resolution is time- and source-scoped. A successful route resolution does not validate content or grant access/redistribution permission.

matrix_notes: NO_DIRECT_ARCHITECTURAL_REFERENCE means no mandatory direct record reference is defined in this contract; it does not prohibit a separately evidenced future relation.
References are authored by the row/source register and point to the column/target register. This direction is normative for the matrix.
Directory Register → Object Identity Register is optional and only allowed after identity is independently established.
Artifact Register → Object Identity Register records what object instance an artifact/version represents or contains.
DeepRead and Integrity each reference the exact source identity and/or artifact version they assess. They do not reference each other as a prerequisite.
Provenance and Rights may reference DeepRead and Integrity event records as supporting evidence, while the event records remain owned by their respective registers.
Route Registry may reference Directory, Object Identity, and Artifact targets. It never references a successful route as proof of access, rights, or semantic validity.

cross_register_invariants: K501 remains the native information model and retains its own object identities, source scopes, temporal references, and status definitions.
Every register is authoritative only for its own record/evidence domain; cross-register links are references, not silent transfers of authority.
Source object identity, artifact identity/version, path/locator, byte sequence, and route are distinct concepts and must not be substituted for one another.
Original source data and derived external representations remain separate.
All records preserve source identity, source scope, time reference, and provenance where available.
Unknown values remain UNKNOWN/OPEN; absence is not FALSE; missing or unresolved references are not silently repaired.
New observations and corrections are append-only; historical records and claims are never silently overwritten.
Validation is not proof of truth, semantic correctness, source completeness, rights, permission, or canonicality.
Integrity evidence is limited to exact bytes and the declared verification scope.
DeepRead evidence is limited to the exact method and extent recorded.
Information loss, unmapped fields, unsupported constructs, transformations, and omissions in external representations must be explicit and traceable.
Routes are navigation declarations only and do not imply target validity, identity, authorization, rights clearance, or semantic correctness.

overlap_decisions.decision: Directory stores observed location/time; Object Identity stores source-object identity. Directory may reference identity only when independently established.
Object Identity identifies a source-object instance. Artifact Register describes a representation/version and references source-object identities. One-to-many is allowed only when evidenced.
Artifact owns description/version; DeepRead owns read event and exact coverage. DeepRead references Artifact and Object Identity; Artifact does not own read status.
Artifact owns description/version; Integrity owns byte/digest evidence. Integrity references Artifact and Object Identity; no reciprocal ownership.
Reading content and verifying bytes are independent operations. Neither implies the other; both may reference the same source/artifact version.
Provenance may reference DeepRead/Integrity events when they support a derivation or preservation claim; those event records remain owned by their respective registers.

overlap_decisions.topic: Provenance vs Rights within one frozen register
overlap_decisions.decision: Keep one register, but distinguish PROVENANCE records from RIGHTS records. No legal permission is inferred from origin, technical access, or a license string alone.
Route stores locator and route resolution; target identity and artifact version are references only. Route resolution does not imply validity or permission.
Define deterministic assignment, source scope, duplicate/copy claims, revision relationship, and evidence required for equivalence before Object Identity schema design.

overlap_decisions.topic: Artifact version and source-object relationship cardinality
overlap_decisions.decision: Define version identity, immutable revision references, and relationship multiplicity in Artifact Register design; do not infer cardinality.
Define how correction, withdrawal, supersession, and status changes are appended without rewriting prior evidence.

overlap_decisions.topic: Directory freshness and route temporal resolution
overlap_decisions.decision: Define observation validity window, stale route handling, unresolved/expired states, and source-interface time semantics.
Define evidence scope, applicable rights/permission statement, reviewer authority, decision time, restrictions, and UNKNOWN/OPEN states. No default legal conclusion.
Define requested vs completed extents, extraction methods, coverage states, and how partial/failed reads are represented without false completion.

overlap_decisions.topic: Integrity algorithm and verification event semantics
overlap_decisions.decision: Define supported algorithms, byte scope, canonical byte acquisition, verifier provenance, and result state per exact verification event.
Define explicit values for unmapped, unsupported, omitted, normalized, defaulted, and lossy fields before any crosswalk or adapter is accepted.
No support or compatibility is inferred from the frozen RO-Crate 1.2 target.

standards.name: JSON Schema
standards.decision_detail: Applies to the structure and allowed value constraints of machine-readable records for all seven registers, Gateway documents, support profiles, and adapter documents. It is structural validation only.
standards.required_clarification: JSON Schema does not establish that referenced IDs exist or that cross-register graph relationships are valid. Referential/graph checking remains a separate validator work unit.
standards.external_boundary: No source truth, identity authority, DeepRead completeness, rights clearance, or canonicality is proved by schema validation.

standards.name: W3C PROV-O
standards.decision_detail: PROV-O Entity/Activity/Agent concepts can represent source/derived entities, read or transformation activities, and responsible agents. K501 identities remain authoritative references; artifact versions and DeepRead events retain their native records.
standards.required_clarification: Add Object Identity Register to the related-register mapping. Keep rights decisions outside PROV-O semantics; provenance vocabulary is not a rights-clearance authority. DeepRead coverage detail remains owned by DeepRead Register.
standards.external_boundary: The PROV-O graph is a derived representation and cannot redefine K501 object identity, source scope, temporal rules, or status values.

standards.name: PREMIS Data Dictionary
standards.decision_detail: PREMIS Object/Event/Agent/Rights entities provide bounded preservation metadata mappings. Artifact and integrity records provide preservation object/fixity information; Provenance and Rights provides rights and responsible-agent evidence.
standards.required_clarification: Add Object Identity Register as the K501 identity reference for PREMIS Objects. The relation is not assumed to be one-to-one. DeepRead events map only when they qualify as declared preservation events; not every read is automatically a PREMIS event.
standards.external_boundary: PREMIS Object identifiers and semantic units do not replace K501 identity or artifact-version definitions. Rights statements in PREMIS do not create legal authority absent source evidence.

standards.name: The BagIt File Packaging Format
standards.decision_detail: Directory observations provide source locators/hierarchy candidates for package payload layout; Artifact Register describes the BagIt package as an artifact; Integrity Register records package-scoped payload and tag fixity checks.
standards.required_clarification: Add Directory Register to the related-register mapping. Provenance/Rights may supply optional bag metadata, but BagIt is not a provenance ontology or rights-clearance mechanism. Any K501 object identifier carried as metadata remains a K501 value, not a BagIt identity.
standards.external_boundary: A complete/valid BagIt claim is limited to the exact bag and files enumerated and checked under RFC 8493. It does not imply Library-wide coverage, semantic correctness, rights, or canonicality.

standards.name: RO-Crate
standards.decision_detail: RO-Crate 1.2 JSON-LD can describe a Root Data Entity, data entities, and contextual entities. It is suitable for selected K501 package/artifact descriptions and context. Directory structure can inform package hierarchy; K501 source IDs may be preserved as external identifiers where appropriate.
standards.required_clarification: Add Directory Register as a source of package/file-structure observations. Remove Route Registry from direct mapped registers: RO-Crate file URLs/identifiers are not equivalent to K501 route declarations or route-resolution evidence. Preserve Object Identity only as K501 identifier references, not as a replaced RO-Crate identity.
standards.external_boundary: RO-Crate 1.2 does not require every file to appear as a Data Entity. It is not a complete Library inventory, file-level identity register, DeepRead record, or K501 route registry. RO-Crate 1.3 remains a separate compatibility review.

support_levels.evaluation_unit: Each result is scoped to exact standard/version + adapter version + operation direction + input/output identity + test fixture/scope. No global standard-level PASS is inferred.

progression.meaning: The exact standard/version and bounded K501 integration purpose are recorded in an accepted, versioned support profile.
progression.limit: A draft or target selection alone is not an accepted registration; this level does not imply a parser or implementation.

progression.meaning: A concrete input document/package is read by an identified parser within the pinned version and scope.
evidence: Exact input identity and byte/scope reference.
Parse result, warnings, and unsupported constructs.
progression.limit: Parsing alone does not establish validation or correctness.

progression.meaning: The parsed input passes the declared syntax/schema/profile checks for the pinned version and profile.
evidence: Validation report, scope, warnings, and result.
progression.limit: Validation is not proof of truth, completeness, rights, identity, or canonicality.

progression.meaning: A versioned K501-to-standard or standard-to-K501 mapping is defined and applied to a declared scope.
evidence: Explicit unmapped, unsupported, defaulted, transformed, and lossy elements.
progression.limit: Mapping does not change K501 native semantics.

progression.meaning: A concrete export or import is performed through a declared adapter boundary. The direction is recorded explicitly; both outcomes may exist for a bidirectional adapter.
evidence: Adapter/version, time, transformation evidence, and losses.
progression.limit: A one-way export or import is not round-trip verification; ROUNDTRIP_VERIFIED requires both directions and a scoped comparison.

progression.meaning: A bidirectional export/import cycle passes declared tests for the exact fixture, fields, and invariants.
evidence: Fixture, expected invariant set, and comparison method.
Observed results, losses, warnings, and report.
progression.limit: Applies only to the tested scope; not universal semantic equivalence or full-system conformance.

support_levels.flow_rule: REGISTERED -> PARSED -> VALIDATED -> MAPPED -> (EXPORTED or IMPORTED); ROUNDTRIP_VERIFIED requires both directions and a scoped comparison. EXPORTED and IMPORTED are distinct directional outcomes, not synonyms.
support_levels.current_achieved_levels: NOT_ASSERTED; profile detail remains a draft until separately accepted.

schema_design_sequence.dependency_note: Define source-object identity, source scope, and explicit equivalence rules first.
Can be designed independently but must cross-reference Object Identity without deriving identity from paths; review alongside order 1.
Depends on stable identity references and exact artifact/version distinction.
References source identity and artifact version; remains separate from Integrity.
References source identity/artifact version and exact byte scope; independent of DeepRead.
Depends on object, artifact, read, and integrity references; retains separate provenance and rights record families.
Depends on registered directory/object/artifact targets and temporal resolution semantics.

acceptance_criteria_for_freeze: Operator explicitly accepts this exact contract revision and its 7x7 directed relationship matrix.
The frozen register names/order and five standard versions remain unchanged.
All required corrections to relationship direction and standard mapping are included in this candidate.
Identity, artifact, read, integrity, provenance/rights, and route boundaries are accepted as written.
Open schema prerequisites remain explicitly recorded and are not converted to implementation claims.
The Markdown and JSON companions pass structural cross-check, exact-byte readback, and SHA-256 verification.

source_basis.scope: Original human gateway; authority is navigation only; identity/source/time/route constraints.
Original machine gateway; route semantics, resolution rules, and source boundaries.
Historical top-level navigation index; incomplete file/content coverage is explicit.
Additive navigation draft; source identity, exact scope, current directory snapshot, and no-mutation boundaries.
Machine route contract and explicit identity/resolution rules.
Role assignments and existing ten directional relationships reviewed; preserved unchanged.
Structured roles, relationship matrix, and source boundaries reviewed; preserved unchanged.
Five frozen support targets and internal support-level model reviewed; preserved unchanged.
Five target versions and related-register lists reviewed; preserved unchanged.
